\caption[ParEval vs held-out pass rate over repair steps]{ParEval vs held-out pass rate over repair steps. Population: STEP[v][k], k = 0, 1, 2 (identical base-cell cohort); unit: base cell; block: composite. Composite block; Q06 correctness pass (solid) and E02 enhanced all-pass (dashed) on the identical base-cell cohort per step (G02 overfitting check); STEP[v][0] == BASE and STEP[v][2] == FINAL[v] (checked). y axis truncated: it starts at 80\%, not at 0 (data-driven lower bound floor((min - 2) / 5) * 5 over the plotted values and CI bounds); the series are dodged horizontally by 0.04 steps so that the error bars do not overlap. error bars: 95\% CI: nonparametric cluster bootstrap, percentile intervals, stratified by block (pilot benchmarks resampled among the 12 pilot benchmarks, full\_ext among its 48); seed 20261017; cluster = benchmark; 2,000 replicates (descriptive, unadjusted). BL01: Includes dense\_la/00 (BL-01 tolerance convention: possible false FAIL verdicts; disclosure-bearing aggregate); sensitivity SA1 in T10. IC1: Q06 is in-sample for test\_feedback and combined\_feedback: their loops see the ParEval test verdict and stop when it passes (every stopped\_tests\_pass trajectory is a Q06 pass), so they optimise the endpoint; for static\_feedback Q06 is out-of-sample (measured once in phase 2, never seen by the loop). The variants therefore differ in trigger and stop rules, not only in feedback content; test\_feedback cannot regress on Q06 by construction. IC2: E02 is not an independent confirmation of Q06 gains: it counts build failures, and most E02 improvements are the same cells as the Q06 improvements; the held-out signal proper is the joint transition X06 (e.g. Q06 repaired but E02 still failing) and G01. IC6: static\_feedback repair triggers are dominated by clang-tidy bugprone findings and, on MPI, by low-confidence hints (design document: no trustworthy static MPI tool exists); static\_feedback results measure this frozen blocking-set configuration, not static analysis in general.}\label{fig:study_analysis_001:F2_heldout_over_iterations}
